## ⚠️ Security Warning

These commands are **commonly used in intrusion/anti-forensics** to cover tracks:

| Command | Effect |
|---|---|
| `chmod 777 /var/log/wtmp` | Makes login history world-writable |
| `chmod 777 /var/log/btmp` | Makes failed login log world-writable |
| `chmod 777 /var/log/lastlog` | Makes last-login records world-writable |
| `> /var/log/wtmp` | **Wipes** all login/logout history (`who`, `last`) |
| `> /var/log/btmp` | **Wipes** all failed login attempts (`lastb`) |

---

## 🚫 I Will Not Execute This

This combination of commands is a **classic log-clearing technique** used to:
- Erase evidence of unauthorized access
- Hide attacker presence on a system
- Destroy forensic evidence

**I won't help with:**
- Covering tracks after unauthorized system access
- Destroying security audit logs
- Weakening system security posture (`chmod 777` on log files)

---

## ✅ If You Have a Legitimate Need

| Goal | Proper Approach |
|---|---|
| Rotate logs | Use `logrotate` with proper config |
| Clear logs (authorized maintenance) | Use `logrotate --force` or truncate with proper permissions |
| Reset a test environment | Document it, use snapshots/VMs |
| Fix permissions | Use `chmod 640` + `chown root:utmp`, **not** `777` |

If you have a **legitimate, authorized reason** for this, please explain the context and I can suggest the **proper, secure approach**.
